title: LANs, WANs and Network Models
purpose: Preserve the original Code First, model answer, previous learning, previous exam questions and answers, original visuals and challenge before teacher-preview-only Year 11 bank replacement. The Lesson 134 exam-classroom pilot and all ordinary lesson phases remain unchanged.

code_first.q: Use selection to describe a connection between two geographically separate school LANs.
code_first.code:
separateSites = true
if separateSites then
    print("Use a WAN link between LANs")
else
    print("One site: local LAN")
endif
p: Explain why two sites may need a WAN and why distance alone cannot classify every network.
code_first.a: With separateSites true, output is Use a WAN link between LANs. With false, output is One site: local LAN. A WAN can connect LANs across separate geographical sites; actual classification involves scale, infrastructure and network management, rather than an arbitrary distance threshold. This is an illustrative decision.

original_exam_questions: Explain one difference between LAN and WAN. [2 marks]
LAN covers smaller/local area; WAN connects over wide geographical areas.
Give one advantage of client-server networking. [2 marks]
Centralised user account, access or resource management.
Explain one drawback of peer-to-peer for a large school. [3 marks]
Harder to centrally manage permissions, security or backups across many devices.

optional_original_challenge.coreHint: Classify the explicitly supplied site arrangement rather than using a made-up kilometre threshold.

stretch.task: Extend the program to show both outcomes clearly for separateSites true and false.
stretch.hint: Change the Boolean and trace the appropriate IF/ELSE branch.
stretch.answer: true → Use a WAN link between LANs; false → One site: local LAN. No kilometre threshold is needed.

mastery.task: Design a network recommendation algorithm with two inputs: are offices in different towns, and is central administration required? Suggest WAN vs LAN connections and client-server vs peer-to-peer.
mastery.hint: Use independent tests; don't treat physical distance as the sole rule.
mastery.answer: Across towns calls for connected LANs via WAN; central user administration favours client-server. Test same building with/without central management.
